can.dice: So fare un gioco da tavolo
can.bake: So aiutare a fare una torta
can.swing: So darmi la spinta in altalena

englishSourceNotes: 'My favorite clothes' is plural while the child circles ONE picture; 'My favorite piece of clothing' / 'thing to wear' matches the task.
'My favorite bug': snail, spider and worm are not insects; fine as US kid-speak, but the category name 'insects and bugs' shows the mix. Italian uses 'bestiolina' (little critter) to stay truthful.
'I can walk a long way' does not match the hiking cue (backpack + poles); 'I can go on a hike' / 'a long walk' is closer.
'I can swing high' — 'high' adds a daring/safety nuance teachers may not want to reward; plain 'I can swing on a swing' is safer. Italian drops 'high'.
'I can help tidy up' is cued by a broom; 'I can help sweep' matches the picture more exactly.
'I can help bake a cake' is cued by activities/baking, which shows a child with pizza/pastry on a board, not a cake.
'I can catch a fish' is cued by a bare fishing rod; fine, but 'I can go fishing' fits the picture without promising a catch.

optionWordFlags.problem: The picture is a live hen; in Italian 'pollo' is what you eat. A child calls the animal 'gallina'.
Correct but formal; a 5-year-old says and reads 'macchina'. Also long to copy.
The picture is a plain slice of bread; in Italy 'toast' means a grilled ham-and-cheese sandwich. 'pane' / 'fetta di pane' matches the picture.
Picture looks like a sprinkled doughnut, and 'bagel' is unfamiliar to most Italian children.
Not an Italian breakfast food; odd choice for 'la mia colazione preferita' (cultural, not linguistic).
English loan, little known to Italian 5-year-olds; the picture could also read as 'riso' or 'yogurt con cereali'.

optionWordFlags.word: ciclismo / pattinaggio / nuoto / calcio vs dipingere / leggere / cantare / sciare
optionWordFlags.problem: Row mixes nouns and infinitives; ideally all infinitives (andare in bici, pattinare, nuotare...) or all nouns. 'ciclismo' is adult/sport register; a child says 'bici'.
Homograph of 'pesca' (peach); the picture (a rod) disambiguates, but a beginning reader may read the fruit.
Picture is only a tent; acceptable, but 'tenda' is what the child sees.
English loans (cupcake, waffle, muffin, pancake) are used in Italy but hard to decode with Italian phonics (cu-p-ca-ke). Not wrong, just hard to copy/read.

otherNotes: Several headings exceed the 22-char target because the shipped pattern itself does ('Il mio animale preferito' = 24). Longest: 'Il mio animale marino preferito' (31) and 'Animale della fattoria preferito' (32); both break cleanly into two lines.
farm heading drops 'Il mio' deliberately: 'Il mio animale della fattoria preferito' is 39 chars and would need three lines.

bird: 'uccello' is the standard school word but has a vulgar slang sense adults may notice; it is used in every Italian primary textbook, so kept. Diminutive 'uccellino' would be wrong for eagle/ostrich.
pet: 'animaletto' chosen over 'animale domestico' (too long) and 'cucciolo' (means puppy/young animal). bug uses 'bestiolina' so the two rows do not share a word.
clothes: 'vestito' avoided because it is also the option word for the dress picture; 'indumento' is the school/science word.
dress: 'So vestirmi' avoids the gendered 'da solo/da sola'. No 'I can' sentence carries gender agreement.
bounce: 'palleggiare' is the precise basketball verb but less transparent for a 5-year-old reader; 'far rimbalzare la palla' is literal and readable.
